source_review.notes: Checked current Kubernetes priority/preemption, disruptions, node-pressure eviction, termination, Kueue, Hadoop Fair/Capacity Scheduler, Slurm, and Flink checkpoint documentation plus primary Borg, Omega, Mesos, and MapReduce publications. All thirteen final cited URLs returned HTTP 200. Product-specific behavior is attributed; the generic cost model and safety workflow state assumptions.

evidence: Reviewed preemptor p, requested vector r_p, free vector f_n, placement n, componentwise deficit Delta, victim v, allocated/releasable vectors r_v/u_v, and eligibility E.
Reviewed lost work L, recovery R, service risk S, fairness debt F, interaction penalty P, release time t, start times T, gross benefit G, and intent I.
Checked CPU, GiB, accelerators, time, item counts, costs, epochs, generations, and componentwise vector comparisons remain explicit.
Confirmed allocated vectors are distinguished from actually releasable vectors and scalar totals are not used as placement proof.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Cost terms require a declared normalization or separate presentation; the chapter explicitly states this.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 victim-set fixture and reproduced deficit (4,6), victims batch-a/batch-b, reclaimed (4,6), and cost 25.
Recomputed the compact example's alternative as one (4,8) victim at cost 40 versus the feasible two-victim cost 25.
Recomputed Exercise 2 node A deficit (4,16), x+y release (6,24) cost 15, and node B z release (8,0) cost 30.
Checked all fixture vectors are scoped to one candidate placement and no cross-node aggregation is implied.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Examples intentionally hold release time, uncertainty, topology, state, availability, and fairness constant.

evidence: Verified Delta=max(0,r_p-f_n) componentwise and victim coverage sum(u_v) >= Delta for a single feasible placement.
Verified G=T_p^0-T_p^V represents earlier predicted start, not completion-time or social-benefit proof.
Checked confirmed release plus reservation is necessary to infer the preemptor can bind; selected or terminating state is insufficient.
Checked generation fencing prevents old victim publication only when every state/output/effect path validates the current epoch.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter separates feasibility and fencing safety sketches from empirical cost/benefit and long-run fairness claims.

evidence: Reviewed zero/large/multidimensional deficits, fragmented resources, one/many/no feasible victims, gangs, devices, volumes, ports, and licenses.
Reviewed no/fresh/stale checkpoints, victim ordinary completion, hung grace, lost notice, slow cleanup, scheduler/node loss, and preemptor cancellation.
Reviewed services, quorum, disruption budgets, leaders, stateful streaming, shuffle producers, local output, external effects, and stale writes.
Reviewed priority abuse, chronic victims, borrowed quota, starvation, reciprocal preemption, restart/checkpoint storms, and degraded capacity.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Authorization, feasibility, availability, data correctness, liveness, fairness, and cost boundaries are reviewed separately.

evidence: Traced preemptor validation through feasible placement, deficit computation, victim filtering/costing, intent, release, reservation, and bind.
Traced each victim through notice, grace, checkpoint/drain, fence, termination, confirmed release, requeue/restore, and terminal recovery.
Checked quorum, disruption, state ownership, residency, security, gang, minimum runtime, entitlement, and resource-vector constraints remain enforced.
Checked victim generations, attempt/output identities, fairness debt, accounting, and in-flight intent reconciliation survive controller restart/rollback.
invariant_checking.notes: Capacity is credited only after runtime-confirmed reuse; suspension and termination requests never imply full release.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from authority and blocked-state proof through victim recovery, outcome measurement, and rollback.
Checked vector coverage proof assumes one placement, actual releases, and reservation against intervening allocation.
Checked fencing proof assumes conditional epoch validation on every state, output, shuffle, and effect publication path.
Checked long-run fairness counterexample where locally cheapest victim selection repeatedly prevents one workload's completion.
proof_review.notes: System safety and fairness depend on explicit protocol assumptions; no optimal victim-selection theorem is claimed.

evidence: Audited preemption, eviction, cancellation, failure, node pressure, reclamation, priority, victim, preemptor, selected, terminating, released, requeued, and recovered.
Confirmed selected/terminating capacity is not mislabeled free or reusable and suspended resources are not labeled fully released.
Confirmed disruption-budget compliance is not mislabeled complete application safety and checkpoint request is not labeled durable checkpoint.
Confirmed preemptor start improvement is not mislabeled cluster-wide benefit or fairness.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Lifecycle terms consistently distinguish control intent, runtime action, resource-ledger state, and application recovery.

evidence: Reviewed decision/release/start latency, vectors, lost work, checkpoint/restore, victim recovery, availability, stale rejects, fairness, congestion, cost, and energy metrics.
Confirmed no universal priority scale, grace period, checkpoint window, victim-count limit, debt weight, cooldown, or benefit threshold is prescribed.
Confirmed the executable fixture tests deterministic set selection only, not runtime release, state safety, prediction quality, or production benefit.
Confirmed production acceptance requires trace replay, fault injection, shadow decisions, class-scoped canaries, hard safety/rate gates, and rollback reconciliation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Evidence must include preemptor, victims, shared dependencies, and other tenants rather than the favored workload alone.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed reason classification, blocked-state proof, per-placement deficits, victim eligibility/cost/set selection, mechanism choice, notice/grace, checkpointing, fencing, actual release, services/gangs/batch/streaming, fairness/borrowing, starvation/abuse, oscillation, observability, and rollout.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable generation-scoped intents, candidate reason codes, vector-aware search, workload preemptibility metadata, bounded grace, checkpoint validation, epoch fencing, ledger confirmation, fallback sets, restart smoothing, debt/accounting, telemetry, canary, kill switch, and in-flight rollback reconciliation. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from policy authority and feasibility through disruption execution and recovery. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover fragmentation, victim cost, suspension, quorum, streaming fencing, gangs, borrowing, controller recovery, externalities, executable selection, classifications, mechanisms, state machines, and rollout.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Kubernetes/Kueue/Hadoop/Slurm/Flink maintainer, Borg/Omega/Mesos/MapReduce researcher, cluster-scheduler operator, data-platform/SRE/security/FinOps specialist, workload owner, affected tenant, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
